true_positives.golden_comment: The downsize method is defined twice. The second definition, which expects a single dimensions string parameter, overrides the first, which expected separate max_width and max_height parameters. This makes the original method unreachable and breaks existing code that calls it with separate width and height arguments.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Duplicate `downsize` definition removes 4-arg API

app/models/optimized_image.rb defines self.downsize twice: at line 145 as downsize(from,to,max_width,max_height,opts) and again at line 149 as downsize(from,to,dimensions,opts). In Ruby the second definition overwrites the first, so any existing caller using the max_width,max_height form now gets ArgumentError (wrong number of arguments). The resize/downsize refactor must support both arities, e.g. with splat args, not two methods with the same name.

true_positives.golden_comment: Hardcoding maxSizeKB = 10 * 1024 ignores Discourse.SiteSettings['max_' + type + '_size_kb'], so the client-side limit can diverge from server-side and per-type settings (also applies to the 413 handler below).
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Client max upload size hardcoded to 10MB ignoring SiteSetting

app/assets/javascripts/discourse/lib/utilities.js lines 182 and 246 replace Discourse.SiteSettings max_image_size_kb / max_attachment_size_kb with hardcoded 10*1024. This breaks admin configurability: instances with smaller or larger limits now validate against the wrong value client-side and show a wrong max_size_kb in the file_too_large error. A file rejected by the server will appear allowed locally and vice versa. Restore use of Discourse.SiteSettings['max_'+type+'_size_kb'] and max_image_size_kb.

true_positives.golden_comment: The loop checking `tempfile.size` may never terminate correctly due to stale cached size, leading to potential infinite loops or incorrect file handling after modifications.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Stale tempfile.size causes unconditional 5x 80% downsizing

app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb line 66 loops while tempfile.size > SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb.kilobytes. tempfile is an open File/Tempfile object modified in place by an external convert process in line 67. File#size on the open descriptor does not reliably reflect the new on-disk size, so the condition can stay true even after the file is already small enough. The result is up to 5 successive 80% resizes (~0.8^5 ~= 0.33 scale) degrading quality and wasting CPU when one pass would suffice. Use File.size(tempfile.path) re-stat after each pass and break when under limit.

false_negatives.golden_comment: Passing 80% as the dimensions can fail for animated GIFs when allow_animated_thumbnails is true, since the animated path uses gifsicle --resize-fit which expects WxH geometry, not a percentage; downsizing would then silently fail.

false_positives.candidate:
API URL download limit hardcoded to 10MB bypassing setting

app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb line 55 changes FileHelper.download(url, SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb.kilobytes, ...) to FileHelper.download(url, 10.megabytes, ...). An admin who configured a small max_image_size_kb to bound bandwidth, disk and ImageMagick CPU can now be forced to download and process up to 10MB per API upload. The limit should remain derived from SiteSetting, with any headroom added explicitly, not a fixed 10MB.

Downsize return value ignored and SVG/vector images corrupted

app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb line 67 calls OptimizedImage.downsize(tempfile.path, tempfile.path, "80%", ...) in a loop without checking its boolean return. If convert fails the code retries 4 more times then uploads the original oversized file anyway. Worse, the guard uses FileHelper.is_image?(filename) which includes SVG, but OptimizedImage.create_for explicitly skips resizing SVG by just copying it because vector-to-raster convert with -resize/[0] mangles or fails on SVG. Downsizing SVG in place can corrupt it or needlessly rasterize it. Skip SVG and break on false return.

true_positives.golden_comment: The EmbeddableHost model's before_validation callback calls self.host.sub! to strip http://, https://, and path segments, but if self.host is nil, this raises NoMethodError.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
before_validation crashes on blank host

In app/models/embeddable_host.rb the before_validation block calls self.host.sub! unconditionally. If host is nil or blank (e.g. admin submits empty host), this raises NoMethodError instead of failing validation. The record can never report a clean validation error and the request 500s.

true_positives.golden_comment: The update and destroy methods in Admin::EmbeddableHostsController do not validate the existence of the EmbeddableHost record retrieved by ID. If EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first returns nil (i.e., the host does not exist), attempting to call methods on the nil object (e.g., save_host or destroy) will result in a NoMethodError.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
update/destroy 500 on missing id instead of 404

In app/controllers/admin/embeddable_hosts_controller.rb update does EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first then save_host(host) without checking for nil, and destroy calls host.destroy without checking. A bad/stale id causes NoMethodError on nil (undefined method `host=' or `destroy') resulting in a 500 instead of a 404 / not-found error.

true_positives.golden_comment: record_for_host compares lower(host) = ? but does not normalize the parameter’s case, so mixed‑case referer hosts may fail to match even though comparison intends to be case‑insensitive.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
case-insensitive host lookup not lowercased

In app/models/embeddable_host.rb record_for_host does where("lower(host) = ?", host) where host is uri.host verbatim. If either the stored value or the lookup URL contains uppercase, lower(host) = 'EVILtrout.COM' never matches. The query must downcase the parameter (host.downcase) to actually be case-insensitive, otherwise host_allowed? incorrectly rejects valid referers.

true_positives.golden_comment: The migration accesses execute(...)[0]['id'] without checking if the query returned any rows, which causes a crash when no embed_category setting exists. This can lead to a broken feature when attempting to edit category/host relationships.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
migration assumes rows exist and crashes on fresh DB

In db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb category_id is derived via execute(...)[0]['id'].to_i without checking for empty results. On a fresh install or DB without embed_category / uncategorized_category_id rows, [0] is nil and the migration raises NoMethodError and cannot migrate. The same applies to the uncategorized fallback lookup.

false_negatives.golden_comment: Because this migration inserts embeddable_hosts rows with raw SQL, any existing embeddable_hosts values that include http:// or /https:// or path segments won’t go through the EmbeddableHost model’s normalization, so the new host lookup (which compares only the bare host) may fail for migrated data. Consider ensuring that migrated hosts are normalized to the same format as newly created EmbeddableHost records so existing embedding configurations keep working.

The contents of `category_fabricator.rb` and `embeddable_host_fabricator.rb` have been swapped, resulting in the loss of original category fabricators and potentially causing errors in fabricator usage.

The SQL query in the `app/controllers/admin/embeddable_hosts_controller.rb` file uses string interpolation (`'#{h}'`) to insert values, which is vulnerable to SQL injection. It should use parameter binding or proper quoting to prevent this security vulnerability.

false_positives.candidate:
SQL injection via string-interpolated host in migration

In db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb the data migration builds INSERT INTO embeddable_hosts ... VALUES ('#{h}', ...) by interpolating the old site_setting value directly. A host containing a quote breaks out of the literal and allows SQL injection / migration failure. It must use quoting/parameterization or sanitize.

_hydrateEmbedded assumes plural ids are always arrays

In app/assets/javascripts/discourse/models/store.js.es6 _hydrateEmbedded now handles xxx_ids by calling obj[k].map directly. If the payload has null, undefined, or a non-array for a plural id key, this throws TypeError and breaks hydration of the whole record. It also leaves undefined entries in the hydrated array when _lookupSubType misses, instead of filtering them.

no uniqueness constraint on host allows duplicates

In app/models/embeddable_host.rb there is no validates_uniqueness_of :host (case-insensitive) and db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb creates the table without a unique index. true_positives.matched_candidate:

false_negatives.golden_comment: Typo in property name: 'stopNotificiationsText' should be 'stopNotificationsText' (missing 'n' in 'Notifications')

false_positives.candidate:
New unsubscribe_link template requires unsubscribe_url for all emails

true_positives.golden_comment: BlockedEmail.should_block_email? method has side effects during a read operation - it updates statistics even when just checking if an email should be blocked. This could cause race conditions in concurrent environments and makes the method name misleading.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Validator has DB write side-effect and non-atomic counter

In app/models/blocked_email.rb, BlockedEmail.should_block? increments match_count/last_match_at and calls save, and it is called from EmailValidator.validate_each on every User validation where email changed. That means a read/validation path writes to the database, updates stats even for validations that ultimately fail or are just probed, and does read-modify-write via match_count += 1 plus save which loses increments under concurrent signups and can fail validation silently.

true_positives.golden_comment: The regex pattern @(#{domains}) in email_in_restriction_setting? method only matches domain suffixes, not full domains with proper boundary anchoring. An attacker can register evil.example.com to bypass a whitelist entry for example.com.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Whitelist/blacklist regex allows suffix bypass

In lib/validators/email_validator.rb, email_in_restriction_setting? builds Regexp.new("@(#{domains})", true) with no end-anchor after escaping only dots. A whitelist entry like allowed.com therefore matches user@allowed.com.evil.com, so an attacker can pass the whitelist (or dodge/match the blacklist incorrectly) by appending a suffix domain, defeating the domain restriction.

true_positives.golden_comment: The case-sensitive email lookup in `BlockedEmail.should_block?` creates a bypass risk, allowing 'User@Example.com' to bypass a block on 'user@example.com'. This can lead to unauthorized access to blocked users.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Blocked-email lookup is case-sensitive and bypassable

In app/models/blocked_email.rb line 12, the lookup is BlockedEmail.where(email: email).first with no downcasing/normalization, and the unique index on blocked_emails.email is case-sensitive. Since email addresses are case-insensitive, an attacker blocked as bad@spammers.org can sign up as BAD@spammers.org or Bad@Spammers.org and BlockedEmail.should_block? will return false, defeating the block.

true_positives.golden_comment: The PollFeed job calls open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url) without validating the URL, allowing an attacker who controls the feed_polling_url site setting to make the server fetch arbitrary internal or external URLs.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Unsafe open() on admin-configured feed URL

Code calls `open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url)` via Kernel#open from open-uri. Kernel#open interprets a leading `|` as a command pipe and follows redirects/SSRF to internal hosts. Must parse/validate the URL and use URI.open with timeouts, not bare open.

true_positives.golden_comment: The current origin validation using indexOf is insufficient and can be bypassed. An attacker could use a malicious domain like evil-discourseUrl.com to pass this check.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Reversed substring origin check on postMessage

postMessageReceived does `discourseUrl.indexOf(e.origin) === -1` instead of comparing origins for equality. Any e.origin that happens to be a substring of discourseUrl (for example a one-character string like `/` or `:`) passes, while the correct check must verify e.origin equals the Discourse origin. This lets a malicious frame resize/inject messages.

true_positives.golden_comment: postMessage targetOrigin should be the origin (scheme+host+port), not the full referrer URL; using the full URL will cause the message to be dropped and prevent resizing.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
postMessage targetOrigin uses full referer URL instead of origin

The second argument to parent.postMessage is `'<%= request.referer %>'` which includes path/query. Browsers require an origin of the form scheme://host:port or *, so delivery with a full URL never matches and auto-resize breaks. It also leaks the embedding page path.

true_positives.golden_comment: Calling `i.content.scrub` assumes that `i.content` is always populated. However, many RSS feeds do not provide a `content` field, leading to a potential nil pointer exception when `i.content` is nil. A fallback to `description` should be implemented to prevent crashes.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Nil feed item content crashes poller

poll_feed does `CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub)` assuming every RSS/Atom entry has content. Items with only link/title/description have nil content, raising NoMethodError and aborting the whole hourly poll so no items are imported.

true_positives.golden_comment: An unescaped request header (request.referer) is interpolated into JavaScript without proper escaping, which can lead to XSS vulnerabilities if the referer contains malicious content. This issue can allow attackers to execute arbitrary scripts in the context of the application.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Reflected XSS via unescaped request.referer in JS

The layout interpolates `<%= request.referer %>` inside a single-quoted JavaScript string without escaping. Referer is attacker-controlled request header, so a value like `');alert(1);//` breaks out of the string and executes script in the embed origin.

false_negatives.golden_comment: The code sets X-Frame-Options: ALLOWALL which completely disables clickjacking protection. The referer validation can be bypassed (referer headers are easily spoofed), and the fallback to empty string for nil referer masks validation failures.

The TopicEmbed.import method is susceptible to a NoMethodError if the contents parameter is nil when attempting to append a string, and an XSS vulnerability due to unescaped url interpolation in the generated HTML.
The ERB block closes with end if, which is invalid Ruby/ERB and will raise at render; it should just be end to close the if block.

false_positives.candidate:
Check-then-create race on embed_url unique index

import does `where(embed_url: url).first` then `TopicEmbed.create!` inside a transaction without handling concurrent creators. Two simultaneous retrieve_topic jobs for the same new URL both see blank and one raises RecordNotUnique on the unique index, failing the job instead of reusing the winner's row.

Non-atomic throttle setnx+expire can leak key

retrieved_recently? does `$redis.setnx(key,1)` then `$redis.expire(key,60)` as two commands. If the process crashes between them the key never expires and that embed_url is throttled forever. Use a single atomic SETEX/SET NX EX.

SSRF and unhandled fetch in import_remote

import_remote does `open(url).read` on an embed_url supplied by any site visitor via EmbedController/TopicRetriever with no host allowlist check at this layer, no timeout, and no rescue. An attacker can make the server fetch internal hosts/files and a single failure or slow origin raises out of the Sidekiq job.

Spec expects TopicRetriever but controller enqueues job

EmbedController#best does `Jobs.enqueue(:retrieve_topic, ...)` while the spec mocks `TopicRetriever.new` and expects `retrieve`. The test does not verify actual behavior and will fail/pass for the wrong reason, leaving the loading path uncovered.

cook_method default is raw_html, converts all existing posts

Migration sets default: 1, null:false. Post.cook_methods is Enum.new(:regular, :raw_html) so regular=0 and raw_html=1. Every existing row backfilled with 1 will hit `return raw if cook_method == Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]` in app/models/post.rb and bypass the markdown/sanitize pipeline, rendering raw markdown source as cooked HTML.

raw_html cook bypass returns unsanitized remote HTML

Post#cook returns `raw` verbatim for cook_method raw_html. TopicEmbed.import/import_remote store RSS/Readability HTML and Disqus content with that flag and render it with `raw post.cooked` in embed/best.html.erb. There is no sanitization, so arbitrary <script>, <iframe>, on* attributes from a feed or scraped page become persistent XSS for every viewer of the topic and embed.

true_positives.golden_comment: -ms-align-items never existed in any version of IE/Edge; the correct legacy property is -ms-flex-align.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Invalid -ms-align-items property emitted

The align-items() mixin in mixins.scss outputs -ms-align-items: $alignment. That property never existed; IE10/11 only understands -ms-flex-align. The invalid declaration is dropped, so IE10/11 falls back to whatever -ms-flex-align resolves to or stretches, meaning @include align-items(center) in header.scss and @include align-items(baseline) in badges.css.scss do not align as intended in those browsers.

true_positives.golden_comment: -webkit-box-ordinal-group and -moz-box-ordinal-group require values starting from 1, not 0. If $val is 0, this will cause incorrect rendering in older browsers, leading to layout issues.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
order() mixin off-by-one for legacy box spec

In mixins.scss the order() mixin emits -webkit-box-ordinal-group: $val and -moz-box-ordinal-group: $val with the same value as order: $val. By definition box-ordinal-group is 1-based while order is 0-based, so box-ordinal-group must be order + 1. As written, @include order(3) in header.scss and @include order(2) in topic.scss produce ordinal-group 3/2 instead of 4/3, so legacy -webkit-box/-moz-box browsers order header panel and extra-info-wrapper incorrectly relative to modern flexbox browsers.

Per CSS flexbox, float and clear on flex items are ignored. The code keeps float: left on .topic-avatar and float: right on button with no flex equivalent such as margin-left: auto or justify-content, so the dismiss button that used to be pinned right will now sit immediately after the text and the avatar/text spacing changes.

Rails serializers expect include_ methods to end with ? for conditional attribute inclusion, a convention followed by other methods in this serializer. Without it, the website_name attribute may not be conditionally included as intended. Additionally, the '.' << website_host string concatenation should be replaced with '.' + website_host or '.#{website_host}' to avoid mutating string literals, which can lead to issues.

Conditional serializer method missing `?` so it never runs

File app/serializers/user_serializer.rb defines `def include_website_name` without a question mark. ActiveModel::Serializers looks for `include_website_name?` (as used for every other conditional attribute in this file, e.g. `include_stats?`, `include_suspend_reason?`). Because the name does not match, the gate is never called, so `website_name` is always serialized even when `website` is blank/nil, contrary to intent.

false_positives.candidate:
Host comparison is case-sensitive and can crash on nil hostname

File app/serializers/user_serializer.rb `website_name` compares `URI(website.to_s).host == Discourse.current_hostname` and calls `discourse_host.split` / `ends_with?` without normalizing or nil-guarding. If `Discourse.current_hostname` is nil/empty the splits raise NoMethodError, breaking user serialization.

File app/serializers/user_serializer.rb adds `:website_name` to `attributes` but does not add it to `untrusted_attributes` (which hides `website`, `bio_*`, `location`, etc. from anonymous viewers for TL0 users via `scope.restrict_user_fields?`). Its own `include_website_name` check only tests `website.present?`. As a result a TL0 user's website host/path is still exposed via `website_name` even when `website` itself is correctly suppressed.

false_positives.candidate:
Group members endpoint allows unbounded limit and negative offset

GroupsController#members does limit=(params[:limit]||50).to_i and offset=params[:offset].to_i with no clamping. A caller can request limit=1000000 to load the whole membership table (DoS/memory) or offset=-5/limit=0 to produce SQL errors or empty results. Clamp limit to a max (e.g. 50-200) and offset to >=0.

add_members does not strip whitespace so comma-space lists fail

add_members does usernames.split(",").each with User.find_by_username(username) and no strip. The user-selector produces comma-separated values that commonly contain spaces ("alice, bob"), so every username after the first fails lookup and is silently skipped, returning success with nothing added. Strip each token and skip blanks.

remove_member bypasses Group membership logic

remove_member does group.users.delete(user_id) then group.save. Direct association delete skips any Group#remove bookkeeping (e.g. primary_group cleanup, counters, callbacks) that the rest of the codebase uses via group.add/group.remove. Use the model removal API so state stays consistent.

false_negatives.golden_comment: The @loaded_locales instance variable in translate_accelerator.rb is lazily initialized and accessed by multiple concurrent threads without synchronization.

Consider normalizing the input locale (e.g., to a symbol) when checking/loading here to avoid double-loading if the same locale is passed as a String vs Symbol (also applies to other locations in the PR).

false_positives.candidate:
Fallback lookup hits SiteSetting and can raise on nil

FallbackLocaleList#[] in config/initializers/i18n.rb calls SiteSetting.default_locale.to_sym on every lookup. I18n::Backend::Fallbacks calls fallbacks[locale] on every translated key, so every I18n.t now touches SiteSetting instead of using a cached chain. Worse, if default_locale is nil or empty the to_sym call raises NoMethodError before uniq.compact can run, breaking all translation with a 500. The lookup should handle nil safely and avoid per-translation SiteSetting access.

Translation LRU cache ignores fallback chain

I18n.translate in lib/freedom_patches/translate_accelerator.rb builds its LRU key as key + config.locale + backend object_id. With the new fallback chain of user locale -> SiteSetting.default_locale -> :en, the same key+locale can resolve differently when the site default locale changes or when different fallback files are loaded, but the cache key does not include the fallback locales. Changing SiteSetting.default_locale will keep serving stale cached strings until LRU eviction, and missing-translation results cached before fallbacks are loaded are frozen in.

ensure_loaded! on every request does redundant locale loads

ApplicationController#set_locale calls I18n.fallbacks.ensure_loaded! on every request, which iterates user locale, site default locale, and :en and calls I18n.ensure_loaded! for each. This runs before preload_json and other translation-heavy work on every request even when the locales are already loaded, adding SiteSetting.default_locale lookups and @loaded_locales scans per request. It also only covers the controller path, leaving other entry points without loaded fallbacks.

translate only loads current locale, not fallbacks

I18n.translate in lib/freedom_patches/translate_accelerator.rb calls load_locale(config.locale) only, while loading of the fallback locales is done separately via I18n.fallbacks.ensure_loaded! called only from ApplicationController#set_locale. Any translation outside a web request (background jobs, mailers, console, initializers, model callbacks) will resolve fallbacks against unloaded YAML files, producing missing-translation strings that are then stored in the LRU cache. The translate path itself must ensure the full fallback chain is loaded.

true_positives.golden_comment: In UsernameForm.authenticate(), isConditionalPasskeysEnabled() is called without passing the required UserModel parameter.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Call to isConditionalPasskeysEnabled() does not match its signature

UsernameForm.authenticate calls isConditionalPasskeysEnabled() with no arguments, but the only definition in the parent UsernamePasswordForm is isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(UserModel user) which requires a user argument. Someone reading only this call cannot resolve it, and javac will fail with cannot find symbol. The re-authentication path in this file therefore does not compile.

true_positives.golden_comment: With isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(UserModel user) requiring user != null, authenticate(...) will not call webauthnAuth.fillContextForm(context) on the initial login page where context.getUser() is still null, so conditional passkey UI will not be set up for first-time passkey login. Consider whether this should also be enabled when no user has been selected yet so ID-less passkey authentication on the initial login form continues to work.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Conditional passkeys now require a known user, breaking usernameless login

isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(UserModel) returns true only when user != null, and authenticate at line 115 and challenge at line 137 now gate webauthnAuth.fillContextForm on that predicate. Previously the form was filled whenever passkeys were enabled, even with no user set, which is exactly what WebAuthn conditional UI / discoverable passkeys need on the initial login page. With this change an anonymous first-factor login gets no ENABLE_WEBAUTHN_CONDITIONAL_UI attribute, no challenge, and no webauth form, so usernameless passkey login/autofill is lost while only the re-authentication case with context.getUser() != null keeps working.

true_positives.golden_comment: The OptimizedCursorPaginator in organization_auditlogs.py attempts to use negative slice offsets on Django querysets, but Django querysets do not support negative slicing and will raise an AssertionError.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Client-controlled negative offset passed to Django queryset slice

src/sentry/api/paginator.py OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_result allows start_offset=cursor.offset when cursor.offset<0 and enable_advanced_features is true. cursor.offset comes from the user-supplied cursor string via Cursor.from_string. Django QuerySet slicing does not support negative indexes and raises AssertionError (Negative indexing is not supported), so a crafted cursor like 0:-100:0 causes a 500 instead of a 400 BadPaginationError as OffsetPaginator/ChainPaginator do. The comment claiming Django handles negative slicing automatically is false.

true_positives.golden_comment: get_item_key assumes a numeric key, but the paginator is used with order_by=-datetime in the audit logs endpoint; calling math.floor/ceil on a datetime will raise a TypeError.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
OptimizedCursorPaginator breaks datetime ordering

src/sentry/api/paginator.py OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_item_key/value_from_cursor copy Paginator numeric logic (math.floor/ceil on value, cursor.value as-is) but src/sentry/api/endpoints/organization_auditlogs.py uses it with order_by="-datetime". For datetime fields value is a datetime, so math.floor(datetime) raises TypeError and integer cursor values are compared against a datetime column in build_queryset, producing wrong queries or crashes. It must subclass DateTimePaginator logic, not numeric Paginator logic.

false_negatives.golden_comment: When requests are authenticated with API keys or org auth tokens (which have user_id=None), organization_context.member is None. Line 71 attempts to access organization_context.member.has_global_access without checking if member is None, causing an AttributeError crash when optimized_pagination=true is used, even though the request passed all permission checks with valid org:write scope.
Importing non-existent OptimizedCursorPaginator

false_positives.candidate:
BasePaginator silently clamps invalid forward offsets

src/sentry/api/paginator.py BasePaginator.get_result changed from queryset[offset:stop] to max(0,offset) for non-prev cursors. Other paginators in the same file explicitly reject offset<0 with BadPaginationError. Silently rewriting a tampered negative cursor to 0 returns the first page instead of an error, hiding invalid cursors and making pagination behavior inconsistent across paginators.

Cursor allows negative offsets without validation

src/sentry/utils/cursors.py Cursor.__init__/from_string accept any int(offset) including negatives with only a comment change. All existing pagination validation assumed offsets are non-negative (e.g. SequencePaginator asserts offset>-1, OffsetPaginator raises on offset<0). Removing that invariant at the shared primitive enables the negative-slice crashes above and invalid prev/next cursors built by build_cursor.

true_positives.golden_comment: OptimizedCursorPaginator's negative-offset branch in get_result() passes cursor.offset directly as start_offset to queryset slicing when enable_advanced_features is True and cursor.offset < 0.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
OptimizedCursorPaginator allows negative slice causing crash or wrong rows

File src/sentry/api/paginator.py line 880 does queryset[start_offset:stop] with start_offset = cursor.offset when cursor.offset < 0 and enable_advanced_features is true. Cursor.offset is attacker-controlled via the cursor string (Cursor.from_string parses int(bits[1]) with no validation). Django QuerySets do not support negative indexing/slicing and raise AssertionError, turning a crafted cursor into a 500, and the comment claiming Django handles negative slicing automatically is false. Even if it did not raise, Python/DB OFFSET semantics would return wrong page. Fix: reject offset<0 with BadPaginationError like OffsetPaginator does.

true_positives.golden_comment: In BasePaginator.get_result(), when cursor.is_prev is True, it sets start_offset = offset without clamping, allowing negative offset values to be passed to queryset slicing.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
BasePaginator passes negative offset through for is_prev cursors

File src/sentry/api/paginator.py line 182 computes start_offset = max(0, offset) if not cursor.is_prev else offset. When cursor.is_prev is true a negative offset is passed directly to queryset[start_offset:stop]. That preserves the old crash/incorrect behavior for prev cursors and contradicts the clamping done for forward cursors. A crafted prev cursor with negative offset causes AssertionError/500 or wrong results. Fix: clamp or validate offset >=0 for both directions.

false_negatives.golden_comment: OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_item_key uses floor/ceil on a datetime key (order_by='-datetime'), causing TypeError.
Accessing .has_global_access on organization_context.member can raise an AttributeError when organization_context is None, particularly for non-superuser non-member users.

false_positives.candidate:
Direct dict access on end_timestamp_precise crashes consumer on missing field

File src/sentry/spans/consumers/process/factory.py line 141 does val["end_timestamp_precise"] with no fallback. Any span event without that field raises KeyError inside process_batch, failing the whole batch, blocking commits and causing backlog/consumer crash-loop. The field was previously optional for tests and the schema may not guarantee it. Fix: use val.get with fallback to message timestamp/now and add validation.

Redirect depth cut from 10000 to 1000 breaks deep segments

File src/sentry/scripts/spans/add-buffer.lua line 30 changed the redirect chase loop from 10000 to 1000 iterations. Traces with redirect chains deeper than 1000 will stop resolving early, leaving set_span_id pointing at an intermediate set. Subsequent ZUNIONSTORE merges then split one logical segment across multiple keys, producing duplicate/incomplete flushed segments. There is no justification for the reduction; restore 10000 or make it configurable.

Removal of max_segment_spans guard hides silent eviction data loss

File src/sentry/spans/buffer.py around line 449 removed the len(payloads)>max_segment_spans check that emitted spans.buffer.flush_segments.segment_span_count_exceeded and skipped oversize segments. The Lua script now silently ZPOPMINs everything over 1000 members. Oversize segments are therefore truncated with no metric/log, max_segment_spans config is dead, and downstream flush will emit incomplete segments while has_root_span/timeout logic still assumes full data. Fix: keep a metric/log for evicted spans and either enforce max_segment_spans or remove the option.

ZUNIONSTORE without AGGREGATE corrupts scores on duplicates

File src/sentry/scripts/spans/add-buffer.lua lines 47 and 53 call ZUNIONSTORE with default AGGREGATE SUM. Scores are end_timestamp_precise. If the same payload member exists in both source sets (retries, duplicate ingestion, overlapping merges) its score is doubled, corrupting ordering and causing the later ZPOPMIN eviction to keep/drop the wrong spans. Fix: pass AGGREGATE MAX (or MIN) explicitly to preserve timestamp semantics.

true_positives.golden_comment: In _set_sample_rate_from_error_sampling(), the check `if client_sample_rate:` treats 0.0 as falsy, so a sample_rate of 0.0 is silently skipped and never set on normalized_data.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Sample-rate test helper swallows errors and mishandles falsy/invalid rates

In _set_sample_rate_from_error_sampling the lookups and float conversion are wrapped in bare except Exception: pass and gated by if client_sample_rate:. This hides malformed contexts, treats 0/0.0 as absent, and accepts out-of-range values like >1 or negative, writing a bad sample_rate into normalized_data that then drives sample_weight in tests.

true_positives.golden_comment: Using Python’s built-in hash() to build cache keys is non-deterministic across processes (hash randomization), so keys won’t match across workers and invalidate_upsampling_cache may fail to delete them. Use a deterministic serialization of project_ids for the cache key.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Unstable cache key built with Python hash()

Line 27 builds the cache key with hash(tuple(sorted(snuba_params.project_ids))). Python's hash() for tuples is salted per-process (PYTHONHASHSEED), so the same project set maps to different keys in different workers/restarts, defeating the shared cache and causing inconsistent behavior. It can also be negative and can collide. Use a stable deterministic encoding such as comma-joined sorted ids instead.

true_positives.golden_comment: The upsampling eligibility check passes the outer dataset instead of the actual dataset used by scoped_dataset. In paths where the query ultimately runs against discover (e.g., dashboard split) while the original dataset is metrics, upsampling may be skipped even when all projects are allowlisted.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Upsampling check uses outer dataset instead of scoped_dataset

_get_event_stats takes scoped_dataset (which the dashboard-split factory changes to discover vs the original dataset) but calls is_errors_query_for_error_upsampled_projects with the outer closure variable dataset. After a split decision the eligibility decision and column transform are therefore made for the wrong dataset, applying upsampling to transaction-like queries or skipping it for error queries.

false_positives.candidate:
Discover error detection misses negated/default error queries

_is_error_focused_query only returns True when the literal string event.type:error appears. The same file's caller and the dashboard-split code issue error queries as (query) AND !event.type:transaction and empty/default queries, which will therefore skip upsampling on discover while the errors dataset upsamples, producing inconsistent under-counts.

Stale allowlist cache returns wrong counts with no invalidation

is_errors_query_for_error_upsampled_projects caches allowlist eligibility for 60s and invalidate_upsampling_cache is defined but never called. A stale True applies sum(sample_weight) (~10x inflation) to projects just removed from the allowlist; a stale False under-counts projects just added. Count correctness must not depend on eventual consistency for a global option lookup.

upsampled_count sums nullable sample_weight and truncates with toInt64

upsampled_count is defined as toInt64(sum(sample_weight)) with no coalesce/default. Rows without sample_weight contribute NULL/0 and are silently dropped from the count, under-counting mixed data, and toInt64 truncates fractional weights (e.g. 1/0.3). The helper even states it assumes the column always exists. Use coalesce/ifNull handling and avoid lossy integer truncation.

true_positives.golden_comment: In BaseDetectorTypeValidator.update(), the validator incorrectly updates instance.type using validated_data.get('detector_type') instead of validated_data.get('type').
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Detector update reads wrong validated_data key for type

update() does `validated_data.get("detector_type", instance.group_type).slug` while create() uses `validated_data["type"].slug` and the serializer field is named `type`. Because `detector_type` is never present, update always falls back to the existing group_type, so changing a detector's type via PUT silently does nothing.

true_positives.golden_comment: Using zip(error_ids, events.values()) assumes the get_multi result preserves the input order; dict value order is not guaranteed to match error_ids, so event data can be paired with the wrong ID (missing nodes also shift alignment).
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Error details misaligned by zipping ids with dict values

fetch_error_details does `zip(error_ids, events.values())` where `events` is the dict returned by `nodestore.backend.get_multi(node_ids)`. Dict value order is not guaranteed to match `error_ids` order, and missing nodes shrink the values list, so titles/messages/timestamps can be attributed to the wrong error id or dropped. The code must look up each node id individually instead of zipping.

true_positives.golden_comment: Hardcoded empty data passed to TableWidgetVisualization causes it to always render an empty table instead of displaying actual results when the feature flag is enabled.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Table widget flag renders empty table instead of real results

When `organization.features.includes('use-table-widget-visualization')` the branch renders `<TableWidgetVisualization columns={[]} tableData={{data: [], meta: {fields: {}, units: {}}}}} />`, discarding `result.data`, `result.meta`, `fields`, loading state and custom renderers. Enabling the flag blanks every dashboard table widget.

true_positives.golden_comment: Validation logic incorrectly uses .get('timestamp'), which treats a timestamp of 0 as absent. It should directly check 'timestamp' in self.initial_data to ensure proper field presence detection, preventing both 'age=0' and 'timestamp' from passing mutual-exclusion validation.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Browser report age/timestamp mutual-exclusion check uses truthiness

validate_timestamp does `if self.initial_data.get("age")` and validate_age does `if self.initial_data.get("timestamp")`. A value of 0 is falsy, so a report with `timestamp: 0` plus `age` passes validation, and a report with `age: 0` plus `timestamp` passes. The check must be presence-based (`"age" in self.initial_data` / `is not None`), otherwise the Working Draft vs Editor's Draft exclusivity is not enforced and invalid mixed reports are accepted.

true_positives.golden_comment: Analytics events are recorded before the feature flag check, resulting in analytics being logged for all requests, including those that return 404 due to the feature being disabled. This can lead to misleading analytics data.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Analytics recorded before feature gate and validation

analytics.record("preprod_artifact.api.assemble") runs before the `organizations:preprod-artifact-assemble` feature check and before body validation. Disabled-feature, unauthorized, and malformed requests are all counted as assemble attempts, polluting metrics. The record call should happen after the feature gate (and ideally after validation).

false_negatives.golden_comment: The BrowserReportingCollectorEndpoint returns HttpResponse objects but the endpoint inherits from Endpoint which expects rest_framework.response.Response objects.

false_positives.candidate:
Merged-PR template calls _truncate_title on wrong class

CommitContextIntegration.get_merged_pr_single_issue_template does `PRCommentWorkflow._truncate_title(title)` but `_truncate_title` is defined as a staticmethod on CommitContextIntegration, not on PRCommentWorkflow. At runtime this raises AttributeError when rendering a merged-PR suspect-issue comment, breaking GitHub/GitLab PR commenting. true_positives.golden_comment: Backup code validation is case-sensitive due to the use of indexOf(). This causes validation to fail if a user enters uppercase hex characters, as backup codes should be case-insensitive for a better user experience.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Backup-code verification is case-sensitive and crashes on non-string

Login does `credentials.backupCode.replaceAll("-", "")` and `indexOf` directly. Generated codes in `setup.ts` are lowercase hex (`randomBytes(5).toString("hex")`) displayed as `XXXXX-XXXXX`, but user input in uppercase or with surrounding whitespace will not match and returns IncorrectBackupCode. Worse, if `backupCode` is an array/object (truthy), `.replaceAll` throws and crashes authorize instead of returning an error code.

true_positives.golden_comment: Because backupCodes are decrypted and mutated in memory before being written back, two concurrent login requests using the same backupCode could both pass this check and update, so a single backup code may effectively be accepted more than once if used concurrently, weakening the intended one-time-use semantics.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Backup-code consumption has read-then-write race allowing reuse

Login reads decrypted `backupCodes`, finds the index, sets `backupCodes[index]=null` and writes back with a separate `prisma.user.update`. Two concurrent logins with the same backup code can both read the same array before either writes, so the same single-use code can be used twice. Single-use codes need an atomic compare-and-set/transaction or DB-level guard.

false_negatives.golden_comment: The exported function TwoFactor handles backup codes and is in BackupCode.tsx. Inconsistent naming.
Error message mentions 'backup code login' but this is a disable endpoint, not login

Object URL for backup codes is not revoked on component unmount, leading to a potential memory leak. This can cause increased memory usage over time, especially if the component is mounted and unmounted frequently.

false_positives.candidate:
Password check bypassed when totpCode is supplied with backupCode

In `authorize`, password verification is gated by `if (user.password && !credentials.totpCode)`. The new branch `if (user.twoFactorEnabled && credentials.backupCode)` is evaluated afterwards. An attacker can send both `totpCode` (any dummy value) and `backupCode`: the first condition is false so no password is verified, the second branch is true so login succeeds on backup-code alone. Backup-code login then becomes single-factor instead of password + backup code, violating the 2FA contract.

Throwing instead of returning 500 breaks error contract

When encryption key is missing or twoFactorSecret is missing/invalid the handler does `throw new Error(ErrorCode.InternalServerError)` instead of `return res.status(500).json(...)`. An uncaught throw in a Next.js API route results in a generic 500 HTML/unhandled rejection, not the `{error: ...}` JSON the client (`DisableTwoFactorModal`) expects. The UI will show generic failure and logs leak, and the same pattern is repeated for the backup-code path.

true_positives.golden_comment: A null reference occurs in GoogleCalendarService.createEvent() and updateEvent() when mainHostDestinationCalendar is destructured from evt.destinationCalendar but evt.destinationCalendar is null or an empty array, causing mainHostDestinationCalendar to be undefined.

true_positives.golden_comment: Logic error: when externalCalendarId is provided, you're searching for a calendar where externalId === externalCalendarId, but this will always fail since you're looking for a calendar that matches itself. Should likely find by credentialId or use different logic.

Collective team calendars silently dropped when organizer has no calendar

evt.destinationCalendar is built as `eventType.destinationCalendar ? [..] : organizerUser.destinationCalendar ? [..] : null` and later `evt.destinationCalendar?.push(...teamDestinationCalendars)` for COLLECTIVE. true_positives.golden_comment: The `appCredentialWebhookRequestBodySchema.parse` function can throw on invalid payloads, resulting in 500 Internal Server Errors instead of the expected 400 Bad Request responses. This can lead to confusion for clients and hinder proper error handling.

true_positives.golden_comment: The addGuests.handler.ts blacklist check uses blacklistedGuestEmails.includes(guest) after lowercasing the blacklist but not the input guest emails, allowing attackers to bypass BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS restrictions by submitting emails with uppercase characters.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Guest dedup and blacklist bypass via case/whitespace

uniqueGuests filters with `guest === attendee.email` and `blacklistedGuestEmails.includes(guest)` but only the blacklist list is lowercased — the incoming guest is not normalized (no trim/toLowerCase). true_positives.golden_comment: The logic for checking team admin/owner permissions is incorrect. This condition uses AND (&&) which requires both isTeamAdmin AND isTeamOwner to be true, but it should use OR (||) since a user needs to be either an admin OR an owner to have permission.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Team admin/owner check requires both instead of either

isTeamAdminOrOwner is computed as `await isTeamAdmin(...) && await isTeamOwner(...)`. A team admin who is not also an owner (the normal case) will fail this check and be denied, while the intent is admin OR owner. The consequence is legitimate team admins cannot add guests; only owners who are also admins (or organizers/attendees via the other clauses) pass. Change && to ||.

true_positives.golden_comment: The sendAddGuestsEmails function in email-manager.ts passes the full calendarEvent.attendees array when determining which attendees receive AttendeeScheduledEmail vs AttendeeAddGuestsEmail, but checks if newGuests.includes(attendee.email) where newGuests is the input guests array.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Email routing uses unfiltered guest list

Attendees are created from `uniqueGuests` (duplicates/existing/blacklisted filtered out) but `sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests)` is called with the original `guests` input. In packages/emails/email-manager.ts new vs existing is decided by `newGuests.includes(attendee.email)`, so a pre-existing attendee re-submitted in the request will be misclassified as new and receive AttendeeScheduledEmail instead of AttendeeAddGuestsEmail, and case differences break the match. Pass `uniqueGuests`.

true_positives.golden_comment: uniqueGuests filters out existing attendees and blacklisted emails but does not deduplicate duplicates within the input; createMany can insert duplicate attendee rows if the client submits repeated emails.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Unbounded guests array with no dedup limit

Schema is `guests: z.array(z.string().email())` with no min/max length, no uniqueness refinement, and no trimming/normalization. A caller can submit hundreds/thousands of emails in one request, creating that many Attendee rows, calendar updates, and outbound emails. The duplicate-within-request case is also not rejected server-side, risking unique-constraint errors or duplicate attendees. Add max length, nonempty, uniqueness and normalization.

false_negatives.golden_comment: Starting with an array containing an empty string may cause validation issues. Consider starting with an empty array [] and handling the empty state in the MultiEmail component instead.

The `sendAddGuestsEmails` function does not check the `disableStandardEmails` flags in the `EventType` metadata, which may result in sending emails to hosts/attendees even when standard emails are disabled for the event type.

Handler only checks NOT_FOUND then permission, never checks booking.status or startTime/endTime. The UI also exposes Edit > Additional guests for past confirmed bookings. Reject non-ACCEPTED/past bookings server-side and hide the action in BookingListItem.

true_positives.golden_comment: Using retryCount: reminder.retryCount + 1 reads a possibly stale value and can lose increments under concurrency; consider an atomic increment via Prisma (increment: 1) to avoid race conditions (also applies to the similar update in the catch block).

Non-atomic retryCount increment loses retries

Both failure paths update with data: { retryCount: reminder.retryCount + 1 } using the value read at the start of the cron run (lines 184 and 195) instead of an atomic increment. If two cron invocations or overlapping executions process the same reminder, one increment overwrites the other, so failures are under-counted and bad numbers are retried forever. Use increment: 1.

true_positives.golden_comment: The deletion logic in scheduleSMSReminders.ts incorrectly deletes non-SMS workflow reminders (e.g., Email, WhatsApp) that have retryCount > 1. Retry-count delete filter deletes non-SMS reminders

The deleteMany uses OR with a second branch of only retryCount gt 1 with no method: SMS constraint (lines 29-45). Once any WorkflowReminder of any method (EMAIL, WHATSAPP) has retryCount > 1 it will be deleted by this SMS cron job, even if it is scheduled for the future and unrelated to SMS. This is data loss beyond the intended SMS cleanup; the retryCount branch must also be scoped to method SMS (and likely scheduled: false).

false_positives.candidate:
Missing sendTo/message never increments retryCount, retries forever

RetryCount is only incremented when twilio.scheduleSMS returns falsy or throws, inside if (message?.length && sendTo). When sendTo is missing (e.g. invalid/missing phone number) or message is empty, the loop does nothing and leaves the reminder unscheduled with unchanged retryCount. That reminder will be re-fetched on every cron run forever, which is exactly the infinite-rescheduling problem the PR claims to fix for invalid numbers.

false_negatives.golden_comment: In getBaseConditions(), the else if (filterConditions) and final else branches are unreachable. This is because getAuthorizationConditions() always returns a non-null Prisma.Sql object, making authConditions always truthy, which means only the first two if/else if conditions are ever evaluated.

Fetching userIdsFromOrg only when teamsFromOrg.length > 0 can exclude org-level members for orgs without child teams; consider deriving from teamIds (which includes orgId) or removing the guard so org-only orgs still include member user bookings.

false_positives.candidate:
OR fragments built without outer parentheses cause precedence bugs

buildFilterConditions builds `("eventTypeId" = X) OR ("eventParentId" = X)` with no surrounding parens, and buildOrgAuthorizationCondition/buildTeamAuthorizationCondition build `(${acc}) OR (${condition})` with no outer parens. getBaseConditions only wraps when both auth and filter exist. If a caller uses the fragment directly as `WHERE ${auth} AND <extra>` or `WHERE ${filter} AND <extra>`, SQL AND binds tighter than OR, so e.g. `a AND b OR c AND d AND e` evaluates as `(a AND b) OR ((c AND d) AND e)` instead of the intended `((a AND b) OR (c AND d)) AND e`, leaking or hiding rows. Fragments containing OR must be parenthesized at construction.

Public findMany method removed without updating callers

The diff deletes InsightsBookingService.findMany (which executed bookingTimeStatusDenormalized.findMany with auth+filter AND) and replaces it with getBaseConditions returning Prisma.Sql. Only two files are changed, so any existing caller still importing/calling findMany will fail to compile or throw at runtime. Removing a public service method is a breaking API change and requires migrating all call sites to $queryRaw with the new conditions.

true_positives.golden_comment: The updateManyByCredentialId call uses an empty data object, which prevents Prisma's @updatedAt decorator from updating the updatedAt timestamp. fetchAvailabilityAndSetCache() in CalendarService.ts calls SelectedCalendarRepository.updateManyByCredentialId(this.credential.id, {}) after every cache population. Passing empty data relies on implicit @updatedAt handling that Prisma updateMany with {} does not guarantee and can reject as empty data, and on success it rewrites every SelectedCalendar row for the credential on every cache refresh just to touch a timestamp the frontend does not even read (frontend uses CalendarCache.updatedAt). true_positives.golden_comment: Throwing a generic Error for authentication failures results in a 500 response in tRPC. Instead, it should return a structured TRPCError with an appropriate code, such as FORBIDDEN, to accurately reflect the error type.

true_positives.golden_comment: Date is formatted with hardcoded 'en-US' locale instead of using the user's locale from useLocale, which can lead to incorrect date representation for users in different locales.

Cache status includes expired rows

Unfiltered credentialIds passed to cache status query

This occurs during booking rescheduling/cancellation, and workflow/workflow step deletion/updates. immediateDelete cancels SendGrid but leaves WorkflowReminder row

deleteScheduledEmailReminder with immediateDelete=true does the SendGrid POST cancel and then returns without deleting or marking the WorkflowReminder row. false_negatives.golden_comment: The 'cancelled' field is nullable, which can lead to existing records having null values instead of a default of false. This can cause incorrect behavior in the application when checking the cancellation status of reminders.

false_positives.candidate:
Cancel-booking reminder cancellations are not awaited

updatedBookings.forEach with nested workflowReminders.forEach invokes async deleteScheduledEmailReminder/deleteScheduledSMSReminder without awaiting or collecting promises. Failures are unobserved and the API can return success before SendGrid/Twilio cancellation or the cancelled=true update has happened, making cancellation unreliable under load or on process exit.

One SendGrid failure aborts all pending email cancellations

The cron loops remindersToCancel with await client.request inside a single try/catch. If any batch_id is null, already sent, or SendGrid errors, the exception jumps to the catch, skips Promise.all for already-queued deletes and skips all remaining reminders. One bad reminder therefore prevents cancellation of all later reminders, so cancelled/rescheduled emails will still be sent.

In handleCancelBooking.ts the paid-booking branch refunds, updates status to REJECTED and returns at req.statusCode = 200 before reaching the workflow-reminder cancellation block at line 485. A cancelled paid booking therefore never marks email reminders cancelled nor cancels/deletes SMS reminders, so scheduled SendGrid/Twilio reminders for that booking will still be sent.

Past-due sweep deletes DB rows without cancelling SendGrid

The handler first does deleteMany where scheduledDate <= now for EMAIL reminders without calling SendGrid cancel. A reminder marked cancelled=true whose scheduledDate passes before the 1-hour cancel window runs (cron downtime, delay, or clock skew) will be deleted from the database but the SendGrid scheduled send remains live, so the email for a cancelled/rescheduled booking will still be delivered.

true_positives.golden_comment: The code uses forEach with async callbacks, which causes asynchronous operations (e.g., calendar/video event deletions, payment refunds) to run concurrently without being awaited. This 'fire-and-forget' behavior leads to unhandled promise rejections, race conditions, and incomplete cleanup, as surrounding try-catch blocks cannot properly handle errors from these unawaited promises. Replace forEach with for...of loops or Promise.all() with map() to ensure proper sequential execution and error handling.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Async deletion in forEach is never awaited

bookingRefsFiltered.forEach(async (bookingRef) => {... await getCalendar ...}) launches an async callback whose returned promise is discarded by forEach. The function then sends the reschedule email and returns true without waiting for calendar.deleteEvent / deleteMeeting to finish, and the surrounding try/catch cannot catch rejections from the async callback. Consequence: calendar/video events may never be deleted or failures are silently lost as unhandled rejections while the booking is already marked rescheduled.

false_negatives.golden_comment: Consider adding try-catch around the await to handle import failures gracefully

false_positives.candidate:
Recurring-cancel apiDeletes populated from unawaited forEach

For recurring cancellation the code does bookingToDelete.user.credentials.filter(...).forEach(async (credential) => { const calendar = await getCalendar(...); ... apiDeletes.push(await calendar?.deleteEvent(...)); }). Because forEach does not await the async callbacks, the later await Promise.all(prismaPromises.concat(apiDeletes)) can run while apiDeletes is still empty. Adding await getCalendar moves the push even later, worsening the race. Consequence: recurring bookings are marked CANCELLED in the DB while external calendar events are never deleted.

true_positives.golden_comment: Incorrect end time calculation using slotStartTime instead of slotEndTime
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Working-hours end check uses slot start instead of slot end

In checkIfIsAvailable both `start` and `end` are computed from `slotStartTime.hour()*60+slotStartTime.minute()`. `end` never adds `eventLength` (unlike `slotEndTime` computed above). A slot starting inside working hours but ending outside is therefore accepted. Combined with the fixed-host filter added by this PR, this allows bookings that overrun working hours and date-override boundaries.

true_positives.golden_comment: Using === for dayjs object comparison will always return false as it compares object references, not values. Use .isSame() method instead: dayjs(date.start).add(utcOffset, 'minutes').isSame(dayjs(date.end).add(utcOffset, minutes))
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Dayjs objects compared with === always false

In checkIfIsAvailable the code tests `dayjs(date.start).add(...) === dayjs(date.end).add(...)` to detect an empty/full-day-block override. `dayjs()` returns a new object every call, so `===` compares object identity and is never true. The intended unavailable-day case is therefore never detected, and a date override meant to block the whole day falls through to the `dateOverrideExist` path and can incorrectly return available.

false_positives.candidate:
Availability re-check uses UTC day/time instead of organizer timezone

checkIfIsAvailable converts the slot to UTC (`slotStartTime = time.utc()`) and then tests `workingHour.days.includes(slotStartTime.day())` and `slotStartTime.hour()/minute()` against per-user `workingHours`, and matches date overrides after an inverted `utcOffset` adjustment (`utcOffset()* -1` then `add`). Working hours and date-override days are defined in the organizer/schedule timezone, not UTC. Near midnight and across timezones the UTC day/hour differs from the organizer-local day/hour, so slots are accepted/rejected on the wrong day and the claimed timezone fix does not hold. It also means a fixed host with no working hours that day matches nothing in `find` and falls through to the busy check returning true, leaving round-robin slots bookable when the fixed host is unavailable.

Date-override day matching and time shift drops day overflow

getSlots selects `activeOverrides` with `dayjs.utc(override.start).isBetween(startOfInviteeDay, startOfInviteeDay.endOf('day'))` where `startOfInviteeDay` is midnight in the invitee timezone, mixing a UTC instant with a zoned day boundary so overrides are attributed to the wrong invitee day. The subsequent offset correction only keeps `hour()*60+minute()` after shifting, discarding any day carry. An override that shifts to the previous/next day in the invitee timezone is therefore rendered on the wrong day or with wrapped hours, and multi-day/cross-midnight overrides are clipped.

true_positives.golden_comment: The code attempts to access integration.metadata[sender][login] without checking for the existence of the sender key. This causes a KeyError for integrations where the sender metadata was not set during creation
true_positives.matched_candidate:

GitHubInstallation.dispatch compares pipeline.fetch_state("github_authenticated_user") to integration.metadata["sender"]["login"] with direct dict indexing. AssignmentSource.to_dict emits non-JSON datetime into Celery task

_ensure_processes_alive only kills when isinstance(process, multiprocessing.Process). In test/thread mode (produce_to_pipe set) and for hung threads, _create_process_for_shards overwrites self.processes/process entry without stopping the old thread. Two threads then run SpanFlusher.main on the same shards concurrently, causing duplicate Kafka produces and races in flush_segments/done_flush_segments. The unused _create_process_for_shard helper has the same leak.

Zero flusher processes possible causes crash / silent data loss

self.num_processes = min(self.max_processes, len(buffer.assigned_shards)) with no validation. If --flusher-processes 0 (or negative) is passed, num_processes becomes 0, then `i % self.num_processes` raises ZeroDivisionError, or if there are zero shards no processes are created and segments are never flushed. The CLI option defaults to 1 but accepts any int. This can crash the consumer on startup or silently drop all segments.

false_negatives.golden_comment: The magic number 50 for max_wait is used repeatedly throughout the tests. Consider extracting this as a named constant to improve maintainability.
The test test_thread_queue_parallel_error_handling has a docstring that doesn't match the test implementation.

false_positives.candidate:
Committable scan loops over full offset range

get_committable_offsets does for offset in range(start, max_offset+1) over Kafka offsets. A single missing offset (gap from filtered/decode-failed or not-yet-seen message) leaves all later offsets in all_offsets forever, so the range grows unboundedly and this runs every second per partition. With large or sparse offsets this is CPU-heavy and all_offsets/outstanding grow without bound (memory leak) blocking all later commits.

Failed work items marked complete and committed

OrderedQueueWorker.run catches all Exceptions from result_processor, logs, and then unconditionally calls offset_tracker.complete_offset in finally. Despite the class docstring claiming only successful processing is committed, poison messages are treated as done and their offsets become committable, silently skipping data instead of blocking/retrying/DLQing.

Offsets committed from background thread

SimpleQueueProcessingStrategy._commit_loop runs in its own Thread and calls the Arroyo commit callable asynchronously every second, while submit/poll run on the StreamProcessor thread. Arroyo expects commit to be called from the processing thread for the owned partitions; concurrent commit during rebalance/shutdown can commit offsets for revoked partitions, race with StreamProcessor shutdown, and mark_committed races across multiple strategy instances sharing the same OffsetTracker.

Partition lock creation is racy

OffsetTracker._get_partition_lock reads and writes self.partition_locks dict without any synchronization. Two threads calling add_offset/complete_offset for a new Partition can both miss in .get() and setdefault different Lock objects, so callers end up holding different locks and all_offsets/outstanding/last_committed are mutated without mutual exclusion. This corrupts committable-offset computation leading to duplicate processing or skipped commits.

Single shared queue pool across partitions/rebalances

ResultsStrategyFactory creates one FixedQueuePool/OffsetTracker in __init__ and reuses it for every create_with_partitions call. Each call then creates a SimpleQueueProcessingStrategy with its own commit thread but sharing the tracker. Each commit thread calls its own partition-scoped commit with committable offsets for all partitions, misrouting commits, and close/terminate of one strategy shuts down the pool still used by other partitions.

close() stops commits before draining workers

SimpleQueueProcessingStrategy.close sets shutdown_event and joins the commit thread, then shuts down the queue pool. Any work item that completes after the commit thread exits will call complete_offset but never be turned into a commit via mark_committed/commit_function. On graceful shutdown processed messages are therefore never committed and will be reprocessed on restart, and there is no final flush.

shutdown clears queue_pool breaking rebalance

ResultsStrategyFactory.shutdown shuts down the pool and sets self.queue_pool to None. Arroyo factories are long-lived and create_with_partitions is called again after a rebalance; create_thread_queue_parallel_worker then asserts queue_pool is not None and fails. The factory cannot serve new assignments after any shutdown/close.

false_negatives.golden_comment: The Check operation exhibits asymmetric cache trust logic: cached permission grants are trusted and returned immediately, but cached denials from the same permission cache are ignored, leading to a fresh database lookup. This allows stale cached grants to provide access to revoked resources, posing a security risk.
The test comment says the cached permissions 'allow access', but the map stores false for dashboards:uid:dash1, so checkPermission will still treat this scope as not allowed.

The cache key construction in `userPermDenialCacheKey` uses simple string concatenation with underscores, which can lead to ambiguous keys and collision risks when any component contains underscores or is empty. This could result in incorrect denial cache hits, affecting user permissions.

false_positives.candidate:
DB fallback still uses stale cached folder tree

Check falls back to getIdentityPermissions when cached scopes miss, but checkPermission/checkInheritedPermissions then calls buildFolderTree which is itself cached in folderCache for shortCacheTTL. If the resource involves a newly created folder or new parent/ancestor relationship, the fresh permission scopes will be evaluated against the old tree, Ancestors(parent) will be empty/wrong, and the check will still deny and then populate the denial cache. The fix for newly created dashboards/folders is therefore incomplete for inherited folder permissions and List results.

Denial cache serves stale denies and is never cleared on allow

In Service.Check the denial cache is checked first (permDenialCache.Get) and on a hit returns Allowed:false without querying the DB, and on a DB-verified deny it does permDenialCache.Set for shortCacheTTL (30s). Nothing ever deletes that entry on grant or on a later allow. So sequence deny -> grant permission in DB (share dashboard, add role/team permission, wildcard grant) -> Check within TTL still hits the denial key (namespace+user+action+name+parent) and denies even though the DB would allow. This reintroduces the exact staleness the PR tries to fix, but in the opposite direction, and prolongs it because the fast-path prevents the DB fallback from ever running until expiry.

Denial key uses raw subject instead of canonical UID

permDenialKey is built from checkReq.UserUID directly from the request subject, while permCache keys are built from resolved store.UserIdentifiers.UID after GetUserIdentifiers (which maps numeric IDs to UIDs). The same user checking as user:123 vs user:uid-string gets different denial keys, so denies can be bypassed or duplicated, and anonymous/render paths are inconsistent with the permission-cache keying.

true_positives.golden_comment: Race condition: Multiple concurrent requests could pass the device count check simultaneously and create devices beyond the limit. Consider using a database transaction or lock.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Count-then-write limit check is racy and unenforceable under concurrency

CreateOrUpdateDevice does CountDevices() then, in a separate session/statement, either updateDevice or INSERT. There is no transaction, row lock, or unique-count constraint. Concurrent anonymous logins can both observe count < limit and both INSERT, overshooting the limit. Conversely two concurrent inserts for the same new device can race. The limit cannot be reliably enforced with this check-then-act pattern.

true_positives.golden_comment: The `tagDeviceUI` function populates the local cache with the device ID before the `CreateOrUpdateDevice` call. If `ErrDeviceLimitReached` is returned, the cache entry remains set, allowing subsequent requests to bypass the device limit until the cache expires after 29 minutes.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Local cache is populated before DB write, letting limit-blocked devices bypass limit

tagDeviceUI() checks localCache, then calls localCache.SetDefault(key) before calling anonStore.CreateOrUpdateDevice(). If CreateOrUpdateDevice fails with ErrDeviceLimitReached, the cache entry remains. The next request for the same new deviceID will hit the cache and return nil without touching the DB, so Authenticate will succeed. A rejected device is therefore only rejected once per ~29m cache TTL and then allowed, defeating the device limit.

true_positives.golden_comment: The updateDevice function returns ErrDeviceLimitReached when rowsAffected == 0, but zero affected rows means the device doesn't exist or falls outside the time window, not that a limit was reached.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Expired devices can never re-register once limit is reached

When count >= deviceLimit, CreateOrUpdateDevice delegates to updateDevice which does UPDATE ... WHERE device_id=? AND updated_at BETWEEN ? AND ?. A device that exists but whose updated_at is older than anonymousDeviceExpiration (30d) matches 0 rows, so updateDevice returns ErrDeviceLimitReached. The count query only counts active devices in the last 30d, so this stale device is not counted but is still rejected and can never be re-inserted/updated. Returning devices after expiry are permanently locked out while the limit is saturated.

false_negatives.golden_comment: Anonymous authentication now fails entirely if anonDeviceService.TagDevice returns ErrDeviceLimitReached. Previously, device tagging was asynchronous and non-blocking. This change prevents anonymous users from authenticating when the device limit is reached.

ProvideAnonymousDeviceService signature breaks DI/wire contract

true_positives.golden_comment: The code uses Error log level for what appears to be debugging information. This will pollute error logs in production. Consider using Debug or Info level instead.

Leftover Error-level logging dumps full ID batches every cycle

Cleanup ticker interval reduced 10x without justification

cleanup.go changes the background cleanup ticker from 10 minutes to 1 minute. The PR description only discusses annotation deadlock avoidance and does not justify running all cleanup jobs (snapshots, dashboard versions, images, invites, short URLs, query history, annotations) 10x more often. false_positives.candidate:
Loop terminates on zero rows-affected instead of zero rows-fetched

untilDoneOrCancelled stops when affected==0. In the new fetch-then-delete split, affected is RowsAffected from DELETE BY IDs. If IDs were fetched (len(ids)>0) but the DELETE affected 0 rows due to concurrent deletion or race, the loop exits as done even though more rows matching the condition may remain. Termination must be based on empty fetch (len(ids)==0), not on delete row count. Consequence is premature stop and leftover expired annotations/tags that should have been deleted in this cycle.

true_positives.golden_comment: The context is being created with d.Log instead of the log variable that was initialized with additional context values (name, kind, method). This means those values won't be propagated to the logging context.

Delete installs wrong logger in context

In `Delete` the code builds `log` with name/kind/method values but then does `ctx = klog.NewContext(ctx, d.Log)` instead of `ctx = klog.NewContext(ctx, log)`. All other methods install the enriched `log`. Downstream storage/legacy calls from Delete lose the per-request fields.

true_positives.golden_comment: In DualWriterMode3's DeleteCollection method, when a storage operation fails, recordStorageDuration is incorrectly called with recordLegacyDuration instead.

Legacy DeleteCollection recorded as storage metric

In `DeleteCollection` the async legacy goroutine calls `d.recordStorageDuration(err != nil, ...)` for the legacy call. It should call `d.recordLegacyDuration`. Legacy delete-collection latency/errors are attributed to storage and legacy metrics are never emitted.

true_positives.golden_comment: Inconsistency: using name instead of options.Kind for metrics recording differs from other methods.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Delete storage metric uses name as kind label

In `Delete` the success path calls `d.recordStorageDuration(false, mode3Str, name, method, ...)` passing the object name where the kind label is expected (error path correctly uses `options.Kind`). This creates high-cardinality / wrong kind labels for delete metrics.

false_positives.candidate:
Async legacy write inherits request context and is cancelled

Create (and Delete/Update/DeleteCollection) spawn `go func()` deriving the async context with `context.WithTimeoutCause(ctx, ...)` where `ctx` is the request context. When the API request completes the request context is cancelled, so the background legacy write is immediately cancelled / times out and legacy silently diverges from storage. The async context must be detached, e.g. derive from `context.WithoutCancel(ctx)` or `context.Background()` with values copied.

Async legacy write races on input object / objInfo

The `go func()` closures capture and use `obj` in `Create` and `objInfo, createValidation, updateValidation, options` in `Update` without a deep copy. The caller may mutate/reuse the object after return and `Storage.Create/Update` may mutate it in place, so the concurrent legacy write races with the caller and can write corrupted/divergent data. A copy must be made before spawning the goroutine, and the returned `created`/`res` object should be the source for legacy, not the pre-storage input.

Storage error recorded as legacy metric

In `Create` when `d.Storage.Create` fails the code calls `d.recordLegacyDuration(true, ...)` with the storage start time. The same mistake is in `Update` at line 129. Storage failures are therefore counted against legacy latency/error metrics and storage metrics miss the failure, corrupting dashboards/alerts for mode 3.

true_positives.golden_comment: The GetWebAssets function implements an incomplete double-checked locking pattern for caching web assets. The function first checks if the cache is populated using a read lock (RLock), and if the cache is empty, it acquires a write lock to populate it. However, it fails to re-check whether the cache was populated by another goroutine while waiting to acquire the write lock.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Exclusive lock held across slow I/O with no re-check

In pkg/api/webassets/webassets.go GetWebAssets takes entryPointAssetsCacheMu.Lock() and then does readWebAssetsFromCDN (network) and readWebAssetsFromFile (disk) while still holding it, and never re-checks the cache after acquiring the write lock. This means every cache miss serializes all other callers, including fast-path cache hits that only need RLock, behind file/network latency, and N concurrent missers will each reload sequentially (thundering herd) instead of one winner populating the cache. Fix with double-checked locking and load outside the critical section: RLock check, unlock, load, then Lock only to publish (with a second check for non-Dev mode).

false_negatives.golden_comment: In addition to the missing double-check, the function has a critical flaw in its error handling: it unconditionally assigns the fetch result to the cache (line 69: entryPointAssetsCache = result) regardless of whether the fetch succeeded or failed. When an error occurs during asset fetching, result is nil, and this nil value overwrites any previously valid cache entry.

true_positives.golden_comment: The enableSqlExpressions function has flawed logic that always returns false, effectively disabling SQL expressions unconditionally:
true_positives.matched_candidate:
enableSqlExpressions always returns false but still dereferences feature flag

pkg/expr/reader.go: enableSqlExpressions computes `enabled := !h.features.IsEnabledGlobally(FlagSqlExpressions)` then returns false on both branches. Since the intent is to unconditionally disable SQL expressions, it should just return false. As written it needlessly dereferences h/h.features, so a nil reader or nil FeatureToggles panics instead of returning the safe 'not implemented' error, turning a blocked query into a crash/DoS, and the inverted negation leaves a trap where a future edit to re-enable will enable when the flag is off.

NoData result immediately overwritten by TableData

Data race on init counter

In searchSupport.init totalBatchesIndexed++ executes concurrently in multiple errgroup goroutines limited by initWorkers with no atomic/mutex protection. This is a data race that corrupts the count reported in the 'namespaces indexed' span event and can be detected by -race. Use an atomic counter or collect results after group.Wait.

NewResourceServer creates a cancelable context for the server, stores cancel in the server struct, then calls s.Init(ctx) synchronously. true_positives.golden_comment: When length starts at -1 from indefinite-length encoding, the arithmetic 'length = length - bytes.length' will behave unexpectedly, potentially leading to incorrect processing of encoded data.
